Disgust can arise around possible contamination or around people and actions judged as deeply harmful or violating Wise Mind values.

## Words describing disgust

Abhorrence, antipathy, aversion, condescension, contempt, derision, disdain, dislike, distaste, hate, loathing, repelled, repugnance, repulsion, resentment, revolted, scorn, sickened, spite, and vile.

## Prompting events and interpretations

Possible events include waste, dirt, blood, contamination, betrayal, abuse, cruelty, degradation, unwanted sexual contact, or conduct that violates Wise Mind values. Interpretations may label something toxic, contaminated, evil, immoral, ugly, or beneath you.

## Body changes, expressions, and action urges

Nausea, gagging, choking, a lump in the throat, faintness, or feeling dirty may occur. Urges and actions include vomiting, washing, cleaning, looking away, pushing away, avoiding, fleeing, attacking, clenching, or speaking with contempt.

## Aftereffects

Attention may stay fixed on what feels offensive or contaminating, with rumination and increased sensitivity to similar cues.

## When disgust fits the facts

Disgust fits when contact could poison or contaminate you, or when a person's behaviour could seriously harm you or a group you belong to.

## Acting on the urge, Opposite Action, and Checking the Facts

When the danger is real, remove or clean the contaminant, stop harmful actions, or avoid harmful people. When disgust does not fit, move close when safe, take in sensory information, act kindly rather than contemptuously, and relax the face and body.
